Container.Name: home-assistant-matter-hub
Container.Overview:
Home Assistant Matter Hub (HAMH) publishes your Home Assistant entities as Matter devices, so Apple Home, Google Home, Amazon Alexa, SmartThings and other Matter controllers can control them locally, with no cloud. This is the actively maintained RiDDiX fork (the original t0bst4r project is archived).
**Required**
1. Create a long-lived access token in Home Assistant (Profile > Security > Long-lived access tokens). 2. Network type must be **Host**: Matter relies on mDNS and IPv6. 3. IPv6 must be enabled in Unraid (Settings > Network Settings > IPv4 + IPv6) and on your router. For VLAN setups give your networks a ULA prefix (fd00::/48); link-local alone does not cross VLANs. 4. Since v2.1, other devices get a 403 on the web UI unless you set a **Web UI Username and Password** below (both or neither). The web UI also accepts IP addresses and local names only; add your reverse proxy host name under Allowed Hosts.
**Setup**
Open the WebUI on port 8482, create a bridge, select entities by domain, label, area or pattern, then pair it with the QR code or pairing code in your Matter controller.
**Troubleshooting**
- Open **Health & Diagnostics** in the web UI. The Network Diagnostics card checks interfaces and mDNS. - Devices pair but show as offline or not responding: limit mDNS to your LAN interface (mDNS Interface = br0 or eth0), and if your LAN has a global IPv6 address controllers cannot reach, set Strip Global IPv6 to true. - If Home Assistant runs as an Unraid VM (or in a br0 container) and its devices go offline, the host may be dropping IPv6 forwarded across br0. Test with `ip6tables -A FORWARD -i br0 -o br0 -j ACCEPT` in the Unraid terminal; if it helps, add it to a User Scripts script that runs at array start. This does not affect the Matter Hub container itself, which uses host networking. - Running an OpenThread Border Router on the same host can cause offline devices across VLANs; see the connectivity guide.
Docs: https://riddix.github.io/home-assistant-matter-hub/ · Connectivity guide: https://riddix.github.io/home-assistant-matter-hub/guides/connectivity-issues

Config.Name: Home Assistant URL
Config.Description: Full Home Assistant URL with http/https and port. Replace the example IP.

Config.Name: Access Token
Config.Description: Long-lived access token from Home Assistant.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Bridges, Matter fabrics and pairings. Back it up: losing it means re-pairing every controller.

Config.Name: Web UI Username
Config.Description: Login for the web UI (no colons). Required for access from other devices since v2.1; set together with the password.

Config.Name: Web UI Password
Config.Description: Password for the web UI. Set together with the username.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Web interface port (host network). If you change it, update the WebUI link in Advanced View too.

Config.Name: Allowed Hosts
Config.Description: Extra host name for the web UI, e.g. matter.example.com or *.example.com (one value). IP addresses, localhost and .local/.lan/.home.arpa/.internal names always work.

Config.Name: Base Path
Config.Description: URL path when served under a sub-path by a reverse proxy, e.g. /matter.

Config.Name: mDNS Interface
Config.Description: Limit mDNS to your LAN interface (e.g. br0, eth0, bond0). Leave empty to use all interfaces.

Config.Name: Strip Global IPv6
Config.Description: Do not advertise global IPv6 addresses over mDNS, so controllers use a locally reachable address.

Config.Name: Refresh Interval
Config.Description: Seconds between scans for new or changed Home Assistant entities.

Config.Name: Node Options
Config.Description: Optional Node.js flags, e.g. --max-old-space-size=768 to cap memory on small systems.
